newsitem.title: UK: EU seen awarding up to 60,000 T sugar at tender.
newsitem.headline: EU seen awarding up to 60,000 T sugar at tender.

text.p: The European Union (EU) is expected to award as much as 60,000 tonnes of current series white sugar at its weekly tender later on Wednesday, traders said.
Early European trading weighed down the dollar, which then recovered as the morning progressed.
"The dollar weakened, which will have dampened enthusiasm for restitutions," said one trader, pegging his tonnage forecast at between 30,000 and 60,000 tonnes.
"But it might not even make the 30,000 tonnes -- it depends who is interested and who isn't," he said.
In its last tender on February 12 the EU awarded 96,500 tonnes of current series white sugar.
Traders estimated this week's maximum restitution level at between 44.008 and 44.028 Ecus (European currency units) per 100 kilos of sugar after the 44.787 Ecus awarded last week.
Licences are currently valid until the end of July.
